caveats:
- I wrote and checked every query myself (an AI); no human has checked them. I read all 456 memories for the 12 personas and used keyword greps across the whole corpus (neighbourhood, university, score, salary, rent, fee, boy/girl, older/younger, EpiPen, Mariza, ski, marathon, race, rowing, jazz, tea, landlord, tournament and others) to confirm that each asked-for attribute is never stated for that persona. For the cross-persona traps, the entity appears only under the other persona: Turin marathon only Sofia, skiing only Jonas, Mariza only Priya, rowing only Priya, jazz night only Jonas, sencha and the language exam only Jonas.
- Some unanswerable questions rest on a false premise (Ines 'the race she signed up for', Tomasz 'Turin marathon', Kwame skiing, Amara 'tea she switched to', Jonas 'rowing club'). A system could fairly answer 'there is no record of that' instead of 'I don't know'. Both should count as refusals, but answer-acceptance metrics that check text may treat them differently.
- I avoided date and duration questions that the session dates make roughly answerable. For example 'when did Priya adopt her dog' and 'how long has Jonas been in the chess club' were rejected. A few remaining ones sit next to stated facts on purpose: the Lantern level count (the prototype had 3 levels), Mateo's cousins ('three evenings a week' is a distractor number), and the Kesho participant count ('first patients').
- In abstention_dev.json, the yes/no answerable rows put the memory phrase as the answer and 'yes' as an alias (e.g. answer 'Dana Whitlock', aliases ['yes','Dana']), so extractive output can match. Short aliases like 'yes', 'no', '12', '2', 'March' and 'week' may give loose matches if the downstream scorer accepts any alias. Tighten them if the scorer works that way.
- Computed answers: Priya rented in Lisbon about 4 years (2021 to March 2025). Jonas's exam was 8 months after moving to Oslo (April 2025 to December 2025). The other 6 computed rows are counts (2 jobs, 2 cities, 2 countries, 2 teas, 2 venues, 2 employers). They are marked computed: true and each has at least two grade-3 gold memories.
- abstention_dev.json uses only p01-p03 memories and does not repeat any benchmark query. Some answerable rows ask about the same memory as a benchmark dev query in different words (e.g. historical fiction, the Afrobeats-style preferences). That is acceptable within the dev split, but the set is not independent of the dev benchmark.
- The checker still flags two entity-level overlaps (brother/Arusha for Amara; Karim/twin for Leila). These are intended distractor entities, not copied wording.
- Helper scripts are in the scratch dir only: tools/new_unanswerable.py (the 30 texts and attribute types), tools/apply_unanswerable.py (edits seed lines in place, keeping formatting and positions), tools/make_abstention_dev.py, and tools/check_abstention_dev.py.
